units: Native and estimated component times in microseconds unless a field says ms or pct.
rules: Ordinary request attribution uses one success per serving DP, the observed request interval, the unique all-layer eager execution matching the prompt shard, the subsequent target graph/eager sequence on all eight ranks, and independently recorded draft verifications. Same graph descriptor on the idle DP does not prove ownership. Draft-token counts are logical. No ordinary hook recorded embedding TASK IDs, physical draft embedding geometry, nonempty SUM, or embedding-bank readers.

Fixed routes keep the existing TP8 SUM and Engram AllGather, fixed placement and model outputs. Shared-local estimates inline half the owner arithmetic and masking for target/draft, remove prezero only if all required elements are overwritten, save half of recorded transpose plus any bound eager final copy if WKV can address the original gathered order, and price gate materializations against local-copy rate and vector budget. Charge new WKV unpack, address, alignment and consumer costs against that saving. No GEMM work removed.

keep_external additionally fuses half its owner arithmetic; skip_external removes the whole graph-external lookup and SUM only on a verified raw-ID/no-other-reader branch. Never credit its owner cost twice. external_only isolates that removal; no such duplicate in frozen eager. SUM uses the last exported completion minus last entry on eight ranks. The generous_named case makes all named owner/transpose/zero/remaining gate-vector work free, plus the same conditional external elimination. This is an illustrative scenario, not a universal ceiling.

All time changes are assumed to reach the client. same_one_wave uses the two eight-rank groups from one frozen tail wave with six external, 24 target/Engram and five draft rows. physical_shape_medians uses 428 common 24-row graph groups for target and the two Engram layers only; external and draft use the two exact tail groups. Those timings are proxies for ordinary requests; the ranges include per-rank cost estimates and both measured ordinary stock latencies, not statistical confidence. Stock percentages use each stock generation’s own request, engine, verification counter and time. Where the other prompt starts during this response, bracket zero or one concurrent eager verification as observed in the instrumented generation; assume the remaining verifications take the observed full graph path. The observed-step millisecond estimate stays separate.

Frozen C8 uses active scheduled waves, retains idle-side target and draft obligations, and brackets the two DPs at each changed lookup or gate. Stop at each request’s prompt wave for TTFT or last own verification for makespan. Full within/across-wave transmission is assumed. These are modelled clock-aligned credits; no new client measurement.

half_gate_and_skip and free_gate_and_skip replace the ordinary traffic term with 50% or 100% of the remaining gate-vector time. They retain the WKV and rotation GEMMs, and keep owner and WKV-input assumptions fixed. These test whether a multi-operator gate could save launch and execution costs above the traffic budget.

Prefill estimate interpolates by scheduled rows between the archived eager TP8 groups, including shorter mixed-wave verification anchors. The two observed eager verifications opposite a new prompt reuse the only frozen six-row eager group. Its peer prompt size and draft geometry differ. Graph runs do not double-count these steps. A service estimate for switching to ReduceScatter/AllToAll is separate and overlaps these costs.
